# Benchmarks

```{r model_family_header, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
acousticTS:::.model_family_header(
  family = "hpa",
  pages = c(
    Overview = "index.html",
    Theory = "hpa-theory.html",
    Implementation = "hpa-implementation.html",
    Benchmarks = "hpa-benchmarks.html",
    Validation = "hpa-validation.html"
  )
)
```

HPA is benchmarked against weakly scattering reference cases to document approximation behavior, not exact modal reproduction.

| Case | Max abs. $\Delta$ TS (dB) | Mean abs. $\Delta$ TS (dB) | Elapsed (s) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Johnson (1977) sphere | 42.20232 | 6.34274 | 0.00 |
| Stanton (1989) sphere | 35.46445 | 5.48942 | 0.01 |
| Stanton (1989) prolate spheroid | 46.13636 | 5.57418 | 0.01 |
| Stanton (1989) cylinder | 46.97943 | 5.65639 | 0.00 |

These large maxima are expected for a high-pass approximation near exact-model nulls. HPA is useful for fast trend and scale checks, not for reproducing fine modal structure.

## Formula reproduction checks

The evaluated HPA formulas are checked against the Johnson and Stanton algebra for the supported high-pass branches [@Johnson_1977; @Stanton_1989_1]. These are formula reproduction benchmarks, not independent full-wave validation.

| Case | Formula branch | Mean abs. $\Delta TS$ (dB) | Max abs. $\Delta TS$ (dB) |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| Sphere | Johnson (1977) | 2.33e-13 | 2.98e-13 |
| Sphere | Stanton (1989) | 3.43e-14 | 4.69e-13 |
| Prolate spheroid | Stanton (1989) | 2.46e-14 | 1.28e-13 |
| Cylinder | Stanton (1989) | 2.39e-14 | 8.53e-14 |
